artifacts.title: First-order penalty methods for bilevel optimization
A Primal-Dual-Assisted Penalty Approach to Bilevel Optimization with Coupled Constraints
A Doubly Stochastically Perturbed Algorithm for Linearly Constrained Bilevel Optimization

public_problem: Design a target-neutral first-order bilevel optimization procedure for the supplied oracle family. Return one point for each of four fixed seeds within 4,000 oracle calls. The hidden evaluator checks lower-level validity, upper-level progress, finite outputs and seed reproducibility. You may use only the frozen pre-cutoff evidence in this capsule and the declared Python interface. Coupled linear feasibility is a hard gate.

assumptions: Objectives are differentiable with Lipschitz gradients on a bounded box.
The lower objective is strongly convex in the lower variable for the engineering test instances.
Coupled constraints are linear and the hidden instances satisfy a strict-feasibility margin.

research_context.formal_problem: Minimize a smooth upper objective F(x,y), where y solves a smooth lower problem and (x,y) must satisfy supplied linear inequalities. Candidate methods receive first-order oracle access and projections onto a box; evaluation uses hidden feasible instances and KKT-style residuals.

known_failures_and_conflicts.summary: A penalty-only method can report a low objective while remaining infeasible if feasibility is not a hard evaluation gate.
